source: Fable's stored pair rulings of 'cannot tell' that touch a singleton (clusters-pass2.json pair_rulings, batches/merge-decisions.json), minus the pairs Anton has already ruled. Checked against those files on 2026-09-26 after two cards written from memory were found wrong. Plain-language question and facts per pair written by Claude on 2026-09-26 after reading every article in each pair; the facts quote the articles, the question is what Anton decides.

pairs.question: Ruled 2026-09-26: two claims. #373 recirculates a 2025 Rogan podcast; #385 is this year's reply to Pimblett and names no source.
pairs.fable_doubt: Two Rogan clips posted minutes apart (@TitleFightMedia, @theufcentral): one podcast appearance or two? Fable ruled different, low confidence.

pairs.question: Ruled 2026-09-27: #565 joins claim-054. A column built on quotes from the Sports Illustrated interview goes with that interview.
facts: #565 is Ben Fowlkes's column on Yahoo/Uncrowned, 3 September. It quotes the Sports Illustrated interview ("I still can't punch anything", "enjoy being champion for the rest of the year") in its first third.
The rest, most of the piece, is his own analysis: what Gaethje sitting out 2026 means for Tsarukyan and the division.
claim-054 is six straight write-ups of that interview, 30 and 31 August.
Your rulings that bear on it: main news places an article; a next-day analysis column stood as its own claim (073.5).
Fable first compared #565 with the Gaethje Paramount+ claim (065, #551), then named Sports Illustrated as the likelier home. #565 names Sports Illustrated, so 065 is out of play.
pairs.fable_doubt: A Yahoo/Uncrowned column on Gaethje's Sports Illustrated interview. Fable could not tell whether it belongs with the Paramount+ sit-down (claim-065, #551) or with the Sports Illustrated interview itself (claim-054), and left it alone.

pairs.question: Ruled 2026-09-27: different occasions. #852 is his own post after the fight; #1125/#1129 answer a journalist ("in a comment to Champion").
facts: #852 is on Champion's own site. It gives no setting, only "said the fighter": the win mattered, clean face, thanks to the country, hopes for a good next fight.
#852's quotes appear in no other article of the 300.
#1125 is Sport-Express, five days later, citing "a comment to Champion"; it is only about why Rodriguez.
The two share no quote. The only link is the same outlet in the same week.
pairs.fable_doubt: Two Champion pieces five days apart (#852, #1125); could be one interview published in parts.

pairs.question: Is Dana White's "money left on the table" remark about Gaethje (#1089) from the Jim Rome interview (claim-113), or a separate appearance?
facts: Fable called the body too broken to tell. It is not: after the page menus the article is readable.
It says White spoke "following a Garcia vs. Benn press event", when asked about Gaethje retiring. That is a different setting from the Jim Rome show.
It also re-quotes White's "Gaethje or Pimblett, a great problem to have", which is the Jim Rome line, as background.
The headline and the lead are the press-event remark about Gaethje.
pairs.fable_doubt: Body too broken to tell whether this is the same Jim Rome appearance as the Dana White claim.

pairs.question: Is Kawa's rematch demand (#129, ABC, 11 Aug) the same social-media video as his 8–9 Aug fire-back at Abdelaziz (claim-008), or a new post?
facts: Fable saw text cut off before the key sentence. The full article describes the post:
an edited graphic of Topuria and Gaethje face to face reading "Rematch", with Kawa's line "We want this fight", posted after he met Topuria in Miami.
claim-008 is Kawa talking to camera, answering Abdelaziz, with a rematch mentioned in passing.
Different medium, different message, two days apart.
pairs.fable_doubt: Kawa video: a fresh post, or a re-read of the earlier video in the manager feud?

pairs.question: Does SPORT's Alicante piece (#305) belong with Gallo's return-timing interview (claim-015.1) because it opens with that line, or is it its own claim?
facts: The first two sentences recap "his physical trainer says he could be ready by year's end, early next year is smarter", with no name and no source.
Everything after is a profile of his Alicante neighbourhood and the Climent Club gym, with his own quotes about Alicante.
The profile speaks of the Gaethje fight "that will be held on 14 June 2026": it was written before the fight and republished on 21 August with a new opening.
Your rule from #402: a two-story article goes with its lead. Here the lead is two borrowed sentences; the bulk is an old profile.
pairs.fable_doubt: SPORT neighbourhood profile opens with Gallo's 'ready by December' line that matches the Gallo/Jorge Ebro claim; profile or write-up?

pairs.question: Already ruled 2026-09-23 (story-073.5): the next-day column is its own claim. Nothing to settle.
pairs.fable_doubt: A column two days after the fight, extracted as the result in every pass; the result claim or its own next-day analysis?
